clue.text: Major source of gold awards written off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of the two words are knocked out of their order and reset

explanation.surface: Prizes for gold production are cancelled, written off as a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written off' reads as one phrase, but 'written' is fodder alongside 'awards' and 'off' alone is the anagram signal. The Witwatersrand is the ridge near Johannesburg, South Africa, that holds the world's largest gold deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Witwatersrand ridge in South Africa has yielded more gold than any other field on earth.

clue.text: Take random iron and drive off *- what a silly pursuit!.'

parts.note: wild means random, as in a wild guess
a goose is a tailor's smoothing iron, named for its curved handle
to chase is to drive away

explanation.surface: Picking up a golf iron and driving wildly is a pointless pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: A tailor's goose is a heavy pressing iron; the golf surface is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A futile errand after something unattainable is a proverbial hopeless pursuit.

clue.text: Compact smashed

explanation.surface: A small car crushed in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact means firmly packed, and smashed is slang for drunk.

clue.text: Team's salvation in trouble? Outside left

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters stand around the abbreviation
in trouble says the letters of the word are in disorder

explanation.surface: A football team pins its hopes on its outside-left winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' scrambles SALVATION and 'Outside' puts it round L. Outside left is an old football position; Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is an English football club, a side in the league.

clue.text: Firm cut in money, perhaps

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
perhaps says the word is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company slashes its spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' scrambles MONEY round CO to give ECONOMY.
explanation.definitionFit: An economy is a saving, a reduction in spending.

clue.text: Being examined in business meeting

definitions.meaning: a session of a council or court

explanation.surface: Someone under scrutiny at a board meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting an exam means taking a test, and a sitting is a session of a court or assembly.

clue.text: Vestment I found in French cathedral town

parts.note: an alb is a white vestment worn by clergy

explanation.surface: A priest finds his robe in a French cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Albi, in southern France, has a famous red-brick fortress cathedral.

clue.text: Quarrelsome type's uprising in faraway situation

indicators.note: in says the rising letters go inside the word for remote

parts.note: distant means far away
the word up, rising, reads upward as PU

explanation.surface: An agitator is behind a revolt in a remote place.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'uprising' means UP written upwards, giving PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A disputant is someone engaged in an argument.

clue.text: Coward's title given by the Duke of Lancaster

definitions.meaning: a play by Noël Coward, not a timid person

definitions.text: given by the Duke of Lancaster
definitions.meaning: words spoken by John of Gaunt in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A play title borrowed from a royal duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Noël Coward wrote a play of this name; John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster, speaks it of England in Shakespeare's Richard II.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward's 1939 play takes its name from Gaunt's patriotic speech praising the English people.

clue.text: Nimble kind of infantry

explanation.surface: A description of agile foot soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-footed means agile on one's feet, and light foot was the name for lightly equipped infantry regiments.

clue.text: This Dutch artist sounds German to Frenchman

indicators.note: sounds says the slang word is spoken and the painter's name heard in it

parts.note: Boche is French slang, offensive, for a German

explanation.surface: A painter's name rings like a French insult for a German.
explanation.walkthrough: Boche was the French soldiers' slur for Germans in the World Wars; Hieronymus Bosch painted 'The Garden of Earthly Delights'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was a painter from the Netherlands famous for nightmarish visions.

clue.text: Board's expression of disbelief

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of incredulity, as in 'oh, go on!'

explanation.surface: What a committee says when it does not believe something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' is a verb, to climb aboard a bus or train; the surface makes it a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on a train is to board it, and 'Get on with you!' is a scoffing retort meaning 'I don't believe it'.

clue.text: Provide this poet, prepacked

indicators.note: prepacked says the poet comes already packed inside the word Provide

explanation.surface: A supplier is asked to deliver a poet ready-wrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Charges directly towards Pole

parts.note: due means directly, as in due north
S stands for the South Pole

explanation.surface: Someone charges straight at a pole, or a Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Dues are fees or subscriptions owed, such as membership payments.

clue.text: The American who wrote it

parts.note: The American is read as a novel title, and the clue asks for its author, himself American-born

explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was the novelist who wrote The American (1877).

clue.text: Dullness of work with a financial centre

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Office work in the money district is a dull affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The City (of London) is Britain's banking and financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is lack of brightness or transparency, a lustreless murkiness.

clue.text: Like daring young man about to turn up round wrecked boat

indicators.note: round says the reversed word goes around the scrambled letters
in a down clue turn up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: circa means about

indicators.note: wrecked says the letters of the word are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A bold young man flips over around a wrecked boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses CIRCA to ACRIC, which goes round OBAT (the anagram of BOAT). The daring young man is the one 'on the flying trapeze' in the song.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's trapeze artist is a circus gymnast, performing nimble feats in the air.

clue.text: Pineapple mainly associated with a tropical island

indicators.note: mainly says most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: pineapple is old military slang for a hand grenade

explanation.surface: Pineapples are grown on a tropical island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fruit is soldiers' slang for a grenade, from its segmented casing; Grenada is a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is an island nation in the Caribbean, within the tropics.

clue.text: Heed panic on part of deerstalker

parts.note: to give ear is to heed or listen
a flap is a state of panic

explanation.surface: A hunter is told to listen out and not to panic.
explanation.walkthrough: A deerstalker is the peaked cap with ties-up side flaps, made famous by Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: The deerstalker hat has fold-down side pieces covering the ears.

clue.text: Country thanklessly takes old wigs

parts.note: Peru is a country

indicators.note: thanklessly says ta, British slang for thanks, is taken out of the next word

explanation.surface: An ungrateful nation steals antique wigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thanklessly' strips TA (British slang for thanks) from TAKES, leaving KES.
explanation.definitionFit: Perukes were the powdered wigs of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

clue.text: Sort of car that is difficult to beat

parts.note: hard means difficult
to top something is to beat or surpass it

explanation.surface: A car model praised as tough to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-top is a motor vehicle with a rigid roof rather than a folding one.

clue.text: This US gangster shortly becomes English outlaw

definitions.text: This US gangster shortly becomes English outlaw

parts.words: This US gangster shortly becomes English outlaw
parts.note: shorten the American word for a thug and it becomes the surname of Sherwood Forest's legendary bandit

explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a violent American criminal; clipped to 'hood' it gives Robin Hood.

clue.text: He is said by rustics to name a goddess

parts.note: taken as written
country dialect uses 'be' for 'is', as in 'he be'

explanation.surface: Country folk name a goddess in their own dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: Stage yokels say 'he be' for 'he is'; Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth, cupbearer to the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth.

clue.text: Head off freight ship

indicators.note: head off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: cargo is freight

explanation.surface: A freight ship is told to steer away.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo carried Jason on his quest for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Bill employed as smooth conman

annotationWithheld.why: Bill employed as smooth conman (5): JACOB is AC (bill) in JOB, but 'employed' must both signal the insertion and supply JOB, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Sort of pin, say, required for surplice

indicators.note: say says the pin's name is spoken aloud and the garment heard

parts.note: a cotter is a kind of pin, as in cotter pin

explanation.surface: A specific pin is needed to fasten a church robe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent COTTER and COTTA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short white surplice worn by choristers and servers.

clue.text: King covered by ace? That's a blow

parts.note: an ace counts as one
R, for Rex, stands for king

explanation.surface: A king trumped by an ace is a blow at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oner' is British slang for a single heavy punch, as in 'hit it a oner'.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is a single knockout punch in British slang.

clue.text: Dressmaker took part in demonstration

definitions.meaning: something that makes a dress, that is a dress fabric

explanation.surface: A seamstress joined a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: A sit-in is a protest where people occupy a place; one who joined it 'sat in'. 'Dressmaker' means the fabric a dress is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy fabric for gowns, and to have sat in is to have joined a sit-in protest.

clue.text: More than half a mile, OK, needs catching up to be in France

annotationWithheld.why: More than half a mile, OK, needs catching up to be in France (9): KILOMETRE ends M + ETRE, but no parse of 'OK, needs catching up' gives KILO; the clue as printed seems to lack a piece
annotationWithheld.clue: More than half a mile, OK, needs catching up to be in France

clue.text: Part of last month's mail for holiday club, perhaps

parts.note: Christmas is a holiday
a club is an example of a playing card

explanation.surface: Letters received in December from a holiday club.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in January, so last month's post was December's; 'club' is a playing-card suit, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal greetings cards make up much of the post in December.
